title: Problem discovery
summary: Read a pile of raw material (interviews, call transcripts, tickets, usage data), pull out the problems people actually have, show the evidence for and against each, and help the person choose which are worth solving.

library.summary: Read interviews, tickets and data, lay out the problems people have with the evidence for and against, and choose which are worth solving.
library.prompt: Find the problems worth solving in {{sources: a folder in context/, or a list of files}} using the problem-discovery skill.

inputs.name: sources
inputs.hint: A folder or list of files: interview notes, transcripts, ticket exports, data tables.

launchers.label: Find the problems in these
launchers.prompt: Find the problems worth solving in {path}.

when: The person has raw material (interviews, call notes, tickets, survey answers, usage data) and wants the problems in it
The person asks what is worth solving, what the pain points or themes are
not_when: Summarising one document or one call
The person already has a problem picked and wants to shape a response to it
routing.needs: A folder or a few files of raw material; context/ is checked first
routing.offer: There is a lot of raw material here. Problem discovery reads all of it and lays out the problems with the evidence for and against each, so you can pick which are worth solving.

start: Run problem discovery on the support calls in context/calls.
Find the problems worth solving in these interview notes.
offer: I've got twelve interview transcripts from last month. What are people actually struggling with?
open: What do you think is behind the spike in cancellations?

invariants: Every problem cites the sources it comes from
Never fill a gap in the sources with a guess
Describe people by segment, never by name
